seo.title: Individual Rental Income Tax Calculator (IRPF, IBS & CBS)
seo.description: Calculate rental income tax for individuals in Brazil. See when IRPF, IBS, and CBS apply for small and large landlords.

page.intro:
The Rental Income Tax Calculator for Individuals by Kitnets.com allows you to simulate, clearly and with up-to-date data, how much tax a landlord really pays on rental income, considering traditional IRPF rules and the new requirements of the Tax Reform (IBS and CBS). 

 With it, you understand: 

 • When rental is taxed only by Income Tax 
 • When the individual is classified as a Large Landlord 
 • When cumulative incidence of IRPF + IBS + CBS occurs 
 • What is the total tax burden and the real effective rate 

 All based on current legislation, especially Art. 251 of the IBS/CBS Law.

whoNeeds.title: Who needs to use this calculator?
list: Real estate investors wanting to understand the tax reform impact
Those evaluating if staying as an individual still makes sense
Those wishing to compare Individual vs Legal Entity/Holding in the future
whoNeeds.footer: If you receive rent as an individual, this calculator is essential.

landlordDistinction.title: Small Landlord vs Large Landlord: what is the difference?
landlordDistinction.intro: The Tax Reform created an important attention point for individuals renting properties.
landlordDistinction.smallText: You continue to be taxed only by IRPF when you do not simultaneously exceed:
smallList: R$ 240,000 per year in gross rental revenue
landlordDistinction.smallFooter: In this case, rent is treated as common taxable income, subject to the progressive Income Tax table.
landlordDistinction.largeText: You are classified as a Large Landlord when, at the same time:
largeList: You possess more than 3 rented properties
Have annual rental revenue above R$ 240,000
landlordDistinction.largeFooter:
In this scenario, cumulative taxation occurs, i.e.: 
 • IRPF continues to be due 
 • IBS and CBS start to apply on rental revenue 
 • **No tax substitution** 
 • **No regime option**
landlordDistinction.conclusion: 👉 The tax burden increases significantly, and that is exactly what this calculator demonstrates transparently.

howItWorks.title: How does the calculator work?
list: Classification rules based on the previous calendar year
howItWorks.footer:
Based on this data, the system: 
 • Determines your legal status 
 • Calculates IRPF due 
 • Calculates IBS + CBS, when applicable 
 • Shows total tax burden 
 • Presents real effective rate, without simplifications

substitution.title: Do IBS and CBS replace IRPF?
substitution.explanation: This is one of the biggest points of confusion today.
substitution.highlight: 👉 IBS and CBS do not replace IRPF.
substitution.text: When applicable, they are added to Income Tax, as they apply to the economic activity of renting, while IRPF continues to apply to the individual's income.
substitution.footer: The calculator makes this explicit, with separate values and consolidated total.

effectiveRate.title: Why can the effective rate seem so high?
effectiveRate.text: Because the individual classified as a Large Landlord starts paying:
effectiveRate.explanation: Even with the 70% reduction in VAT rate for residential rental, the combined burden can easily exceed 30% of revenue, depending on the taxpayer's profile.
effectiveRate.footer: 👉 This is the exact point where many investors start evaluating a Legal Entity or real estate holding.

transparency.title: Transparent simulation, no unrealistic promises
transparency.footer: This calculator was built to inform and plan, not to mislead.

important.title: Important to know
list: Classification as Large Landlord is based on the previous calendar year
In some cases, IBS/CBS incidence may occur in the current year, according to law
VAT credits are not considered in this version
The result is a simulation, does not replace an accountant or tax lawyer

interestRateConverterPage.title: Monthly and Annual Interest Rate Converter
interestRateConverterPage.metaDescription: Convert monthly interest rates to annual and annual to monthly using compound interest. Free and accurate tool.
interestRateConverterPage.intro: Convert monthly interest rates to annual rates and annual rates to monthly rates automatically and accurately using compound interest — the same method used by banks and financial institutions. This converter is ideal for comparing mortgages, investments, rents, loans, and any contract using interest rates over different periods. Simply enter the rate in one field to instantly see the equivalent rate for the other period, without manual calculations or incorrect approximations.
interestRateConverterPage.supportingText: Unlike simplified conversions that merely multiply or divide the rate by 12, this tool considers the real effect of compound capitalization, ensuring correct and reliable results. For example, a 1% monthly rate is not equivalent to 12% per year, but rather 12.6825% per year. If you are analyzing a mortgage, rent adjustment, investment return, or any financial simulation, this converter helps standardize rates and make more informed decisions.
interestRateConverterPage.educationalNote: Note: Conversions use compound interest. A monthly rate of 1% is not equivalent to 12% per year.

items.question: How to convert monthly interest to annual?
items.answer: The compound interest formula is used, raising the monthly rate to the 12th power to get the effective annual rate: i_a = (1 + i_m)^12 - 1.

items.question: Does this converter use simple interest?
items.answer: No. All conversions use compound interest, reflecting real financial market practices.

igpm.title: IGP-M Today: Complete History, Charts, and Rent Adjustment
igpm.description: The IGP-M (General Market Price Index) is one of Brazil's most important economic indicators, widely used for adjusting rent contracts, school tuitions, energy bills, and various services.
igpm.pageDescription: On Kitnets.com, track IGP-M updated monthly, with complete historical data since 01/01/1995, interactive charts, monthly heatmap, and detailed tables for accurate and reliable analysis.

sections.title: What is IGP-M?
sections.text: The IGP-M is an inflation index calculated monthly by Fundação Getulio Vargas (FGV). It measures price variation at different economic stages, from production to final consumption, which explains its high sensitivity to exchange rates, commodities, and global economic shocks. Due to this scope, the index became known as 'rent inflation', being the reference for millions of contracts in Brazil.

sections.title: How is IGP-M calculated?
sections.text: The calculation of IGP-M is based on a weighted average of three sub-indices, each representing a distinct stage of the economy:

items.title: 📦 IPA – Broad Producer Price Index (60%)
items.text: Monitors wholesale prices, with strong influence from agricultural commodities, industrial goods, and exchange rate variations.

items.title: 🛒 IPC – Consumer Price Index (30%)
items.text: Tracks price variation of goods and services consumed by families.

items.title: 🏗️ INCC – National Construction Cost Index (10%)
items.text: Reflects costs of materials, labor, and services in civil construction.

items.title: 📅 Collection period
items.text: From the 21st of the previous month to the 20th of the reference month, allowing for faster capture of recent price variations.

sections.title: IGP-M Today: track in real time
sections.text: On Kitnets.com's IGP-M page, you find:

items.title: Intuitive Visualization

sections.title: IGP-M History since 1995
sections.text: Kitnets.com provides one of the most complete historical IGP-M series, ideal for analyzing old contracts, simulating rent adjustments, economic and academic studies, and real estate investment decisions. You can explore the index evolution over decades and identify cycles of rise, stability, and deflation.

sections.title: IGP-M Evolution Chart
sections.text: The interactive chart allows you to visualize monthly index variation, periods of high inflation, deflation phases, and the impact of economic crises and global cycles. This visualization facilitates understanding the index behavior over time.

sections.title: IGP-M Monthly Heatmap
sections.text: The heatmap presents IGP-M behavior month by month, year by year, with intuitive colors helping to quickly identify high inflation months, deflation periods, seasonal patterns, and index volatility. It is a powerful tool for analyzing contract adjustments and historical trends.

sections.title: IGP-M and Rent Adjustment
sections.text: IGP-M is widely used in rental contracts in Brazil. Its impact is direct: high inflation leads to more aggressive adjustments, while deflation can lead to reduced or even negative adjustments. Therefore, tracking the index is essential for owners, tenants, real estate agencies, and investors who want to negotiate contracts fairly and informed.

sections.title: IGP-M or IPCA: which is better?
sections.text: In recent years, many contracts have switched from IGP-M to IPCA due to IGP-M's high volatility, especially during periods of exchange rate and commodity shocks. On Kitnets.com, you can easily compare different indices and understand which makes more sense for each type of contract.

selic.title: Selic Rate: Complete History Since 1995 and Copom Decisions
selic.description: The Selic Rate is Brazil's main monetary policy instrument and directly influences interest rates, inflation, credit, investments, and economic growth. All interest rates in the country — from real estate financing to fixed income investments — have the Selic as their central reference.
selic.pageDescription: On this Kitnets.com page, you can follow the complete historical series of the Selic Rate since January 1995, the starting point of the Real Plan, with up-to-date data, interactive charts, monthly heatmaps, and detailed tables for short, medium, and long-term analysis.

sections.title: What is the Selic Rate?
sections.text: The Selic is the basic interest rate of the Brazilian economy, defined by the Central Bank of Brazil. It represents the average rate of one-day financing backed by federal government bonds, traded in the Special System for Settlement and Custody (Selic).
sections.footer: In practice, the Selic serves to:
list: Define the attractiveness of fixed income versus other assets

sections.title: Selic Historical Series Since the Real Plan (1995)
sections.text: Kitnets.com provides the Selic historical series since January 1995, allowing analysis of:
list: Interest rate behavior across different governments
Cycles of inflation fighting and economic stimulus
Periods of structurally high and low interest rates
The impact of Selic on investments, real estate, and fixed income
sections.footer: This long history is essential to understand how monetary policy has shaped the Brazilian economy in recent decades.

sections.title: Copom Decisions: How Selic is Defined
sections.text: The Selic Rate is defined by the Monetary Policy Committee (Copom), a Central Bank body responsible for establishing the basic interest rate at each cycle of meetings. Copom meets eight times a year and, at the end of each meeting, announces the new Selic target, along with a statement explaining the rationale for the decision.

sections.footer: 📌 The Copom minutes are published at 8:00 AM on the Tuesday following each meeting, providing a more detailed analysis of the economic scenario, inflation, economic activity, and risks considered by the committee.

sections.footer: These visualizations help investors, property owners, and analysts understand the impact of Selic on financing, yields, and long-term decisions.

sections.title: Selic, CDI, and Real Estate Market
sections.text: The Selic directly influences the CDI, real estate financing, government bonds (Tesouro Selic), and the cost of credit for families and companies. In periods of high Selic, fixed income tends to compete strongly with real estate investments; in cycles of decline, real estate credit becomes more accessible and the property market gains traction. Therefore, following the Selic is fundamental for financial planning, investment analysis, and real estate market decisions.

panoramaPage.title: Panorama Econômico do Brasil: inflação, aluguel e juros em um só lugar
panoramaPage.description: O Panorama Econômico do Kitnets.com reúne, em uma única página, os principais indicadores econômicos do Brasil, organizados de forma clara e visual para facilitar a análise de inflação, aluguéis, juros e investimentos.
panoramaPage.intro: Aqui você acompanha a variação mensal e o acumulado dos últimos 12 meses dos índices oficiais mais utilizados no país, com gráficos intuitivos que permitem identificar tendências, ciclos econômicos e mudanças relevantes no cenário macroeconômico.

sections.title: Indicadores de Inflação
sections.text: A inflação impacta diretamente o custo de vida, contratos, reajustes e o poder de compra. No Panorama Econômico, você encontra:

items.def: Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor, o principal indicador oficial de inflação do Brasil, utilizado pelo Banco Central.
Índice Nacional de Preços ao Consumidor, focado em famílias de renda mais baixa e amplamente usado em reajustes salariais.
Índice Geral de Preços do Mercado, tradicionalmente conhecido como “inflação do aluguel”, muito presente em contratos imobiliários.

sections.conclusion: Cada índice apresenta sua variação no mês mais recente e o acumulado em 12 meses, permitindo comparar rapidamente o comportamento da inflação sob diferentes metodologias.

sections.title: Indicadores de Aluguel e Mercado Imobiliário
sections.text: Para quem investe, administra ou aluga imóveis, entender a dinâmica dos aluguéis é fundamental. O Panorama Econômico inclui:

items.def: Indicador de preços de imóveis e aluguéis nas principais cidades brasileiras.
Índice de Variação de Aluguéis Residenciais, focado exclusivamente na evolução dos valores de locação.

sections.conclusion: Esses indicadores ajudam proprietários, inquilinos e investidores a avaliar se os reajustes de aluguel estão acima ou abaixo da inflação e como o mercado imobiliário está se comportando ao longo do tempo.

sections.title: Juros e Investimentos
sections.text: As taxas de juros influenciam diretamente financiamentos, rendimentos e decisões de investimento. No Panorama Econômico do Kitnets.com, você acompanha:

items.def: A taxa básica de juros da economia brasileira.
Referência para a maior parte dos investimentos em renda fixa no Brasil.

sections.conclusion: Com a visualização do acumulado em 12 meses, fica mais fácil comparar o desempenho da renda fixa frente à inflação e aos reajustes de aluguel.

sections.title: Detalhamento completo de cada indicador
sections.text:
Ao clicar na seta (➝) localizada no canto superior direito de cada cartão, você acessa a página detalhada do índice selecionado.

Nessa página, é possível consultar informações completas como:
list: Filtros por período (mensal, anual e acumulado)
Gráficos interativos com evolução ao longo do tempo

sections.conclusion:
Esse recurso permite sair de uma visão resumida do panorama econômico para uma análise aprofundada, ideal para quem precisa tomar decisões financeiras, acompanhar reajustes de aluguel, analisar inflação ou comparar indicadores ao longo dos anos.

changes.title: What changes in Income Tax in 2026?
changes.intro: Starting January 2026, the most significant IRPF changes in recent decades come into effect:

items.title: Total exemption up to R$ 5,000 per month
items.text: Those receiving up to R$ 5,000 in monthly taxable income may have zero tax, even if the progressive table indicates tax to pay. This happens through a legal reduction of up to R$ 312.89, limited to the calculated tax amount.

items.title: Partial reduction between R$ 5,000 and R$ 7,350
items.text: Taxpayers in this range are not fully exempt but pay less tax, with a decreasing and linear reduction that diminishes as income increases and zeroes out exactly at R$ 7,350.

items.title: Above R$ 7,350
items.text: For higher incomes, the calculation follows the progressive table normally, without additional reduction application.

holdingRentalPage.title: Holding Rental Tax Calculator (Presumed Profit)
holdingRentalPage.intro:
The Brazilian Tax Reform has profoundly changed how property rentals will be taxed starting in 2026. With the creation of the Dual VAT (IBS + CBS), many landlords, investors, and family holdings face real doubts about how much tax will be paid, when PIS/COFINS cease to exist, and how the tax burden evolves over time.

This calculator was created exactly to answer these questions clearly, transparently, and in alignment with legislation.

whatItDoes.title: What this calculator does
whatItDoes.p1: The Holding Tax Calculator (Presumed Profit) allows you to estimate, in detail, the tax burden on property rentals when leasing is conducted by a Legal Entity, structured as a family holding, opting for Presumed Profit.
list: PIS and COFINS (only in 2026, during the transition)
CBS and IBS (Dual VAT), with a 70% legal reduction for real estate operations
The official Tax Reform transition schedule (2026–2033)
whatItDoes.p2: All this in a single simulator, with annual or monthly views, charts, and complete breakdown.

targetAudience.title: Who is this calculator for?
list: Property owners renting via family holding
Families structuring assets in a Legal Entity
Anyone wanting to understand if the Tax Reform increases or reduces rental taxes

howToUse.title: How to use the calculator (step by step)

steps.title: 1️⃣ Choose the reference year (2026 to 2033)
steps.text: Use the timeline slider to select the desired year.
bullets: 2026: transition year (PIS/COFINS still exist; CBS and IBS start being charged at reduced rates)
2027 onwards: PIS/COFINS are extinguished; Only Dual VAT (CBS + IBS) remains
steps.note: This allows you to clearly visualize the impact of the tax transition over the years.

steps.title: 2️⃣ Enter your rental revenue
bullets: Annual Revenue: enter the total amount received in the year
Monthly Revenue: enter month by month (ideal for those with rental variations)
steps.note: The calculator automatically identifies if there is an Additional IRPJ (10%) incidence, which occurs when monthly revenue exceeds R$ 20,000.

steps.title: 3️⃣ (Optional) Adjust the nominal VAT
steps.text: By default, the simulator uses a nominal VAT of 28%, within the currently discussed range (26.5% to 28%).
steps.attention: Attention: The calculator does not apply 28% directly to the rent. It follows the correct rule of the law: First divides VAT into CBS and IBS, Then applies the 70% legal reduction for real estate rentals, Only then calculates the effective amount to pay

sections.title: 📌 Taxes on Profit (Presumed Profit)
sections.text: The calculation base is 32% of gross revenue. Upon this base apply:
list: If monthly revenue exceeds R$ 20,000, Additional IRPJ of 10% is automatically applied on the excess

sections.title: 📌 Taxes on revenue (consumption)
sections.text: In 2026 (transition): PIS: 0.65%, COFINS: 3.00%, CBS and IBS start being charged at reduced rates. From 2027: PIS and COFINS are extinguished; Only Dual VAT (CBS + IBS) remains

sections.title: Legal reduction for properties
sections.text: Legislation provides for a 70% reduction in CBS and IBS rates for property rental operations. In practice, this means that a nominal VAT of 28% results in a much lower effective rate, correctly applied by the calculator.

resultsDesc.title: What you see in the results
list: Separation by groups: Taxes on profit, Dual VAT, Legacy taxes
resultsDesc.note: Additionally, there is a complete breakdown with calculation base, nominal rates, reductions, and annual values.

important.title: Important to know
list: ❌ This calculator does not consider IBS/CBS credits, for prudence
✅ Calculations follow a conservative and educational approach
📊 Ideal for planning and understanding, does not replace accounting advice
important.disclaimer: Legal notice: simulator for educational purposes. Consult your accountant before making decisions.

whyUnique.title: Why this calculator is different
whyUnique.text: Unlike many superficial contents about the Tax Reform, this tool:
list: Respects the correct order of Dual VAT calculation
Considers the real transition between PIS/COFINS and CBS/IBS
Correctly applies the 70% reduction for properties
Shows the impact over time, not just in an isolated year
whyUnique.conclusion: If you rent properties through a family holding or are evaluating this structure, this calculator helps you understand, compare scenarios, and prepare for the new Brazilian tax system.

article.title: Minimum Tax Calculator for High Income (IRPFM)
article.intro: The Kitnets.com Minimum Tax Calculator for High Income (IRPFM) allows you to simulate, clearly and in detail, how much minimum tax an individual taxpayer may pay on income if their annual earnings exceed R$ 600,000, according to the rules introduced by Law No. 15,270/2025, valid from the calendar year 2026.
article.description: This new taxation was created to ensure real progressivity at the top income level, even when a significant part of the earnings consists of dividends, exempt income, or exclusively taxed income.

whatIs.title: What is the Minimum Tax for High Income?
whatIs.content: The IRPFM (Minimum Individual Income Tax) establishes that taxpayers with high annual income must pay a minimum effective rate, calculated on the aggregate income received in the year, including:
list: Other taxable, exempt, or exclusive income
whatIs.note: Even with exemptions, legal deductions, and traditionally untaxed income, those exceeding the R$ 600,000 annual limit enter the minimum tax regime.

howItWorks.title: How does the IRPFM rate work?
howItWorks.content: The minimum tax rate is progressive and linear:
list: Up to R$ 600k/year → exempt from IRPFM
Between R$ 600k and R$ 1.2M → rate grows gradually from 0% to 10%
howItWorks.note: The calculator automatically shows the effective rate applied, according to the entered value.

whatToSimulate.title: What you can simulate with this calculator
list: See if your income falls under the minimum tax
Correctly apply: Legal exclusions (capital gains, inheritance, RRA, etc.) and Permitted deductions (savings, indemnities, specific exemptions)
Consider: IR already paid in annual return, Withheld IR, Tax paid abroad, Definitive IR already collected, and Anticipated IRPFM on dividends
Visualize the final IRPFM payable or zero, transparently

dividends.title: Dividend taxation: how does it enter the calculation?
dividends.content: The law also provides for monthly anticipation of IRPFM when dividends paid by the same company to an individual exceed R$ 50,000 in the month, with 10% withholding at source. This withholding is not a definitive tax: it enters as a credit in the annual minimum tax calculation — and the calculator automatically considers this adjustment.

redutor.title: IRPFM Reducer: protection against double taxation
redutor.content: To prevent the sum of taxes paid by the company (IRPJ + CSLL) and the individual from exceeding certain limits, the law created the IRPFM reducer. In the calculator, this reducer can be entered simply, allowing simulation of scenarios where: The total tax burden was already high on the legal entity or The individual's minimum tax is partially reduced or even zeroed.

list: Explicit legal basis at each step of the calculation
Clear interface, with summary of base and tax
Ideal for financial and tax planning
Integrates with the logic of other Kitnets.com tax calculators

pageContent.intro:
The Pro-Rata Rent Calculator allows you to accurately calculate the rent due when the contract does not cover a full month, a widely common situation at the beginning, ending, or early termination of a lease.

With just a few details — rent amount, start date, and end date — you find out exactly how much should be paid, avoiding errors, disputes, and improper charges.

sections.title: 📅 When is pro-rata rent used?
list: Tenant entry after the month starts
sections.text: In these cases, rent must be calculated proportionally to the days effectively occupied.

sections.title: 🧮 How calculation works?
sections.text: The calculation follows simple logic widely used in rental contracts:
list: Determine daily rent value (By commercial 30-day month or real days)
Multiply: Daily Value × Number of Days
sections.conclusion: The result is the exact pro-rata rent to be paid.

sections.title: ✅ Why use Kitnets.com Calculator?
list: Ideal for tenants, owners, and agencies
sections.text: The calculator shows not only the final value but also daily value, days considered, and exact period.

sections.title: ⚖️ Is it mandatory by law?
sections.text: The Tenancy Law (Law No. 8.245/91) does not define a single formula, but proportional calculation is widely accepted and usually foreseen in contracts.
sections.conclusion: This calculator helps exactly with that.
